findings.title: join() breaks before terminating remaining flusher processes
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.join, if the shared deadline has already passed when the loop reaches a process, the loop executes `break` before reaching `process.terminate()`. Because `self.next_step.join(timeout)` runs first and can consume the whole timeout, this can result in *no* flusher processes being terminated at all; if one process consumes the deadline, later processes are also skipped. On shutdown this can leave hung/running flusher processes alive (e.g. still producing to Kafka) after the consumer believes shutdown finished. The loop should still terminate every process, using the deadline only to bound how long each wait takes.

findings.title: Invalid flusher process counts are silently accepted
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as “unset” and falls back to all shards, while a negative value survives the `or`. A negative `--flusher-processes` then makes `self.num_processes` negative, so `process_to_shards_map` and `_create_processes()` create zero flusher processes. `SpanFlusher.submit()` will still forward messages to `next_step` (CommitOffsets), so consumer offsets can be committed while no segments are ever flushed. Validate or clamp `flusher_processes` to at least 1 before constructing the flusher.

findings.title: New wait in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 does not actually wait. The comment says it is giving the flusher thread time to process after the drift change, but it provides no synchronization. As a result the test can race with the background flusher before `step.join()` sets the stopped flag, making it flaky or allowing false positives. Use a synchronization primitive that is not patched out, or limit the monkeypatch to the flusher's sleep call.

findings.title: New multiprocess flusher test never exercises real processes
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` passes `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`. In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, the presence of `produce_to_pipe` forces `make_process = threading.Thread`, so the new test only asserts the internal shard map/count while running threads. The actual production path introduced by this PR—`multiprocessing` spawn, pickling each shard buffer and shared Values, killing/restarting a real process, and parallel flushing from multiple processes—is not covered. A regression in process startup, restart, or shutdown could therefore pass this test suite.

findings.title: Inserting flusher_processes before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
findings.body: `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` previously took `produce_to_pipe` as the sixth parameter; the new `flusher_processes` parameter is inserted before it. Any existing caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now bind that callable to `flusher_processes` and leave `produce_to_pipe` as `None`, causing `SpanFlusher` to try to use the callable as a process count (and to start multiprocessing instead of the pipe/thread path). Either keep `produce_to_pipe`’s original position or make callers use keyword arguments consistently.
